title: Teacher agency in the age of generative AI: towards a framework of hybrid intelligence for learning design
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the question of how generative AI (genAI) affects teachers’ professional agency in educational settings. Rather than evaluating a specific tool with experimental data, the authors discuss the risks that genAI may reduce teachers’ capacity to act, affect decisions, and take stances when it is used for learning design, lesson creation, grading, and related educational tasks.

The paper situates this discussion within broader debates about educational technology adoption, teacher trust in AI, and the tendency for edtech to prioritize learner agency while limiting teacher influence over the technology. It draws on concepts from teacher agency, contextual knowledge in TPACK, and hybrid intelligence to argue that AI systems should be designed as human-AI collaborative partners rather than autonomous substitutes for teachers.

The proposed approach is a theoretical framework in which hybrid intelligence supports co-creation between teachers and genAI so that teachers retain agency while benefiting from AI assistance. The paper uses prior literature and conceptual arguments, with illustrative examples such as genAI supporting learning design and tailoring explanations for learners. Its main conclusion is that genAI should be designed to extend, not diminish, teacher agency, and that human-centred hybrid intelligence may help align AI use with educational and ethical goals.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI/LLM chatbot systems used for educational purposes such as content generation, lesson design support, feedback, and adaptive explanations.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper discusses genAI as a broad class of tools that can support teachers’ learning design, provide feedback, generate teaching materials and lesson plans, and act as a human-AI collaborator; it is not an empirical evaluation of a specific product.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical paper about teachers’ agency and hybrid intelligence, not an empirical study of an AI tool. It does not report controlled, quasi-controlled, or subgroup analyses.
impact_tier_rationale: No outcomes are measured, so there is no evidentiary estimate of impact. The paper proposes a framework rather than demonstrating effectiveness or differential effects.
